The study finds that 95.5 percent of trips had no fault, while 2 percent of trips had fault value of 1 and 1.25 percent of trips had fault value of 2&3 each. It was also found that the average distance for fault occurrence of values 0,1,2 and 3 were 3.4, 2.8, 4.0 and 3.8 kms respectively.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology for Medical Records Security Using Fit Viability Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: For patients, accurate and comprehensive medical records are an incredible asset. During medical services, privacy protection and the integrity of sensitive medical information are critical concerns. Blockchain technology, renowned for its immutable and decentralized nature, presents a promising solution to safeguarding these critical records. This research paper delves into the patient perspective concerning the utilization of blockchain to fortify healthcare document security. In addition, the blockchain’s properties were assessed concerning the healthcare supply chain using the Task Technology Fit (TTF) framework and the Fit-Viability Model (FVM). An empirical study of 296 customers/patients and healthcare professionals from medical sector shall evaluate fit and viability of blockchain technology adoption for storage and protection of medical records. The Fit and Viability framework was analyzed implementing structural equation modelling to access the adoption of blockchain technology in medical sector. Research findings indicate that task-technology fit, and environment technology fit significantly influenced functional benefits and symbolic benefits respectively. Further function benefits and viability had significant positive impact on BCT adoption. However Symbolic benefits were found to be insignificant for BCT adoption. In conclusion, this research advocates for a paradigm shift in healthcare document security, emphasizing patient empowerment and trust through blockchain technology. By centering on patient perspectives, concerns, and preferences, this paper advocates for the adoption of blockchain solutions having a significant impact due to functional benefits that not only fortify document security but also prioritize consumers/patient’s confidence and participation in their healthcare journey.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Attention U-Net for Optic Disc and Optic Cup Segmentation in Retinal Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This research illustrates the Multi-Scale Attention UNet (MSA-UNet) architecture to develop the retinal fundus image segmentation employing effective capturing complex features. The research innovation points mainly include the continuous integration of multi-scale image convolution layer and attention gate. The strategic integration of the decoder path and the developed superior performance compared to existing art of segmentation networks. The decoder path is split into two major paths. One represents the integration of attention gates and multi-kernel convolution. Another indicates the development of double $3 \times 3$ convolution for up sampling. The proposed research design not only enables the network to capture the complex features efficiently, but also leveraging attention mechanisms overwhelm irrelevant areas that improve the segmentation precision. This research mainly includes the ORIGA and REFUGE datasets to realize the superior performance of MSA-UNet. It is evident that employing the proposed Multi-Scale Attention UNet (MSA-UNet) architecture, the retinal fundus image segmentation significantly improved. The research has practical implication in the medical image analysis, particularly in the retinal fundus image segmentation with maintaining high precision. As a result, research may contribute to the diagnosis and treatment of retinal diseases, such as glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy.

articleTitle: Hate Speech Detection System using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Hateful comments and speeches on social media platforms have emerged as a significant and disturbing issue in recent times. With the rapid modernization of the internet, the proliferation of such content has also increased swiftly. Addressing this problem requires substantial efforts within the sector, particularly in the development of hate speech detection techniques. One effective approach involves the utilization of efficient machine learning models. This paper proposes a model dedicated to the detection of hate speech. The chosen dataset undergoes thorough preprocessing and cleaning, enhancing the quality of the text. Further exploration of the cleaned text aims to provide a more comprehensive understanding. Key features are extracted from the dataset to facilitate model training, incorporating lemmatization, stemming, and the removal of stop words to eliminate unnecessary data. The model is built using CountVectorizer, and various machine learning algorithms are employed to assess performance and gain insights for model improvement. By implementing effective preprocessing techniques and optimizing hyperparameters, our model has demonstrated superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 96%.

articleTitle: Towards a Pervasive Paradigm: Enabeling Patients Privacy Through Decentralized Identity and Data Control in E-Health
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Patient care has certainly enriched by implementing digitalization in healthcare. This digital transformation has posed obstacles with data security and privacy. By the introduction of e-health, huge volumes of sensitive and classified data is digitally processed and the likelihood of numerous personal health records (PHR) rules infractions or breaches has drastically increased by implementation of digitalization. Even with the advancement in technologies, it will take due time before a system development can effectively address the security issues and give patients, who are the natural guardians of their health data a total control over their personal data. Hence, there is an urgent need for a patient-centric system that maintains data privacy and gives patients a total control over their PHR. To redefine E-Health security, the cutting-edge technologies comprising of Distributed Hash Table (DHT), Blockchain, Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI), and Inter Planetary File solution (IPFS) needs integration. IPFS and DHT enables in improving Data privacy by providing a reliable and effective decentralized and distributed storage solution. Enabling safe access control over this information, a Decentralized Ledger Technology (DLT) leverages the transparent and unchangeable characteristics of Blockchain. The idea of SSI, which gives patients control over their digital identities and to manage their E-Health data, is fundamental to this paradigm. This study advocates for the widespread implementation of patient-powered electronic health record management system. Additionally providing encouraging paths to improve data security and privacy in the domain of digital healthcare.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Analysis and Exploitation Attacks on Smart Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Wearable devices are becoming more popular these days due to its unique features and its effectiveness. The evolution of Internet of Things (IoT) that combined health care devices and sensors has entirely changed the scenario in the healthcare infrastructure. This innovation will confidently improve the existing healthcare facilities and practices due to the continuous observing of patient’s health even in the remote places. Regardless of their effectiveness, IoT devices are insecure and are vulnerable to security threats that should need to be overcome. The main issue is to protect from outside entities or attacks that may obstruct the advancement and put the individual’s information at risk. This study focuses on outlining the vulnerabilities focusing on smartwatches in the healthcare IoT domain. Furthermore, it has been observed that a limited Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) based smartwatches has a very weak or no security defense system making these devices vulnerable to various security threats such as Brute-force attacks, Man-in-The-Middle (MiTM) attacks, Denial of Service (DoS) attacks, and Phishing. Experimental testing has been performed to test the vulnerabilities in smartwatch devices to verify the data integrity concerns. By using Bluetooth sniffing tools, the security of the smart wearable devices has been tested to identify its weaknesses and to target the BLE devices. Attempts have been made to tamper its parameters by gaining access to the devices through Bluetooth connection. The overall result reveals that these devices are vulnerable to different exploits. This study provides the foundation to assess possible vulnerabilities in smart wearable devices. Furthermore, it highlights the loopholes existed in these devices which can be exploited.

articleTitle: Ayurvedic Herb Classification using Transfer Learning based CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: For approximately over 4000 years, medicinal herbs are being utilized in traditional medicine. Ayurvedic herbs have gained popularity in medical industry due to their fewer side effects and lower costs compared to modern medicine. However, it’s difficult for agronomists and pharmaceutical companies in the biomedical domain to identify the suitable herb leading to the loss of age’s old Ayurvedic knowledge. This paper aims at implementing a system that examines an Ayurvedic leaf using Transfer Learning based Convolution Neural Networks (CNN). Ayurvedic Herb recognition is based on their images. The experiment considers 1835 images of Herbs across thirty species of healthy medicinal plants. The success rates for Herb identification were found to be as high as 98.97% in testing accuracy for DenseNet121 Convolution Neural Network. VGG16, MobileNetV2 and InceptionV3 models reported a test accuracy of 93.79%, 96.21% and 97.59% respectively. Additionally, the future research will be further focused on dataset expansion to benefit agronomists and stakeholders thus enriching about knowledge of Ayurvedic Herbs.

articleTitle: Ethnos: An Ethereum-based Online Social Networking System with Two-Factor Authentication and Trust Score
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: As social media grows to entangle and remould the lives of people, so grows the concern over data privacy, censorship, server outages, and control over personal information by proprietary bodies due to their centralized design. The rise of blockchain has encouraged researchers to consider the decentralization framework for developing online social networks to resolve the challenges mentioned above. In a decentralized ecosystem, no one entity has absolute access to data and the power to enforce arbitrary decisions. The benefits of this include ownership over personal data, censorship resistance, data security, and improved control over user-generated content. In this paper, we propose the design of Ethnos, a social networking application built to harness the powers of blockchain and distributed storage technology to heighten the security and reliability of users as well as their data. In that context, suitable smart contracts have been fabricated. This paper also prospects integration of two-factor user authentication and trust score checks with Ethnos to corroborate the trustworthiness of both user and data. In addition, Ethnos incorporates a remuneration system to compensate users for their contribution to and engagement with the platform.

articleTitle: cryptoRAN: A Review on Cryptojacking and Ransomware Attacks W.R.T. Banking Industry - Threats, Challenges, & Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In the banking industry, ransomware is a wellknown threat, but since the beginning of 2022, cryptojacking, an emerging threat is posing a considerable challenge to the banking industry. Ransomware has variants, and the attackers keep changing the nature of these variants. This review paper studies the complex background of these two threats and scrutinizes the actual challenges, and problems that the banking industry and financial institutions face. These threats, though distinct in nature, share commonalities, such as financial motivations and sophisticated techniques. We focus on examining the newly emerged variants of ransomware while we provide a comprehensive idea of cryptojacking and its nature. This paper involves a detailed breakdown of the specific threats posed by cryptojacking and ransomware. It explores the techniques cybercriminals use, the variabilities they look for, and the potential consequences for financial institutions and their customers. This paper also finds out how cybercriminals change their techniques following the security upgrades, and why financial firms including banks need to be proactive about cyber threats. Additionally, this paper reviews the background study of some existing papers, finds the research gaps that need to be addressed, and provides suggestions including a conclusion and future scope on those disputes. Lastly, we introduce a Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) approach for up-to-date cyber threat hunting processes for minimizing both cryptojacking and ransomware attacks in the banking industry.

Author Keywords: digital forensics and incident response approach

articleTitle: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Personalized Elderly Care through the lens of the Hedonic Motivation System Adoption Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This research aimed to create and evaluate a hedonic motivation model to comprehend elderly citizens’ acceptance of generative artificial intelligence. The age-related cognitive ability traits and perceived boredom of the elderly were added to the earlier technology acceptance model in the proposed hedonic motivation and flow model. The theoretical model was empirically evaluated using survey questionnaire data of 314 respondents over 55 years. The result showed that cognitive ability significantly impacted perceived ease-of-use, impacting all five hedonic variables. Flow experience was impacted by curiosity and joy but not by control. It was also found that perceived usefulness did not impact usage, while boredom and flow experience impacted usage of GAI-assisted personalized elderly care. The study stated implications for theory and practice before concluding with future research directions.
